claims.text: The local catalog and selected Pokumon/Bulbapedia snapshot place the CoroCoro Comic January 1998 issue promo insert on December 15, 1997.
The source slice models two promo identities for the January 1998 CoroCoro issue: Meowth (CoroCoro 1997) and Computer Error (CoroCoro, Pokemon Song Best Collection CD 1997).
The selected snapshot says CoroCoro Comic's January 1998 issue was published with two promo cards, Meowth and Computer Error.

Computer Error is the load-bearing variant row: Bulbapedia separates the glossy CoroCoro/Song Best Collection prints with red drop shadow on the Team Rocket R from the later Kamex Mega Battle participation print with non-glossy stock and white drop shadow.

The local catalog preserves Meowth as a parent source-pinned row and Computer Error as a manual provider-path row for the glossy CoroCoro/Song Best print lane, explicitly not reusing the later Kamex Mega Battle UPC/45 row.
The local row credits Ken Sugimori for Meowth and Sumiyoshi Kizuki for Computer Error. These remain source/provider metadata, not physical-card proof.

This CoroCoro insert is small but unusually instructive: Meowth is the mascot-like magazine freebie, while Computer Error is a rules-card gag that later becomes a variant maze across CoroCoro, Song Best, Kamex, and English Wizards Promo memory. The issue shows CoroCoro as a distribution machine where cute character pull and mechanical TCG weirdness could travel together.

Agents should preserve CoroCoro January 1998 issue route, December 15 1997 date, Meowth row 030, Computer Error row 031, glossy/red-drop-shadow Computer Error lane, Song Best reprint association, and Kamex non-equivalence before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: CoroCoro January 1998: cute mascot, broken machine
narrative.why_it_matters: This two-card insert has real charm because it splits the magazine brain perfectly. Meowth is the character hook: recognizable, Sugimori-clean, binder-friendly. Computer Error is the system joke: a trainer card about machinery going sideways, later tangled into one of the best tiny variant puzzles in early Japanese promos. Together they show CoroCoro not merely advertising Pokemon, but distributing little pieces of how Pokemon felt: cute, strange, mechanical, collectible.
